To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temporal scale (seasonal and interannual) is more important than spatial scale (farm location and within-field variability) in determining the abundance and infectivity of the leafhopper vector.

the temporal scale is the most important scale at which ecological process are driving aster leafhopper population dynamics and that the seasonal pattern of aster leafhoppers is similar to that of the pathogen infectivity.
the temporal variability of leafhopper abundance was higher than the spatial variability and that the infectivity of the insect was highly correlated with the time of the year.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the relevant scale at the level of which ecological processes are responsible for aster leafhopper and AYp spread, and the use of this information for the design of effective pest management strategies.
identifying and characterizing the ecological processes that influence AYp spread, and our results suggest that the temporal scale of these processes is more important than the spatial scale.
the development and application of multilevel modeling techniques for the evaluation of spatial and temporal covariates of pest population dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AYp spread in Wisconsin carrot fields is primarily driven by temporal variation in leafhopper abundance, which in turn is driven by weather and climate factors.
the temporal and spatial factors that affect aster leafhopper population abundance and infectivity in Wisconsin are not constant and are not the same across years.
the aster leafhoppers' seasonal pattern and infectivity are not synchronized and that the seasonal patterns of both are not consistent across the years of this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal covariates were the most important factors influencing aster leafhopper populations and AYp infectivity.

the most important factor for the management of AY disease is the control of the leafhopper vector, and the most effective way to control leafhoppers is to use insecticides at the right time and at the right place.
AYp spread and the associated risk of AY disease is a function of both the abundance and infectivity of the leafhopper.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal scale at which processes are occurring is more important than spatial scale in determining aster leafhopper and infectivity.
temporal processes are the most important in determining leafhopper abundance, while both temporal and spatial processes are important for determining infectivity.
the seasonal pattern of aster leafhoppers and their infectivity is relatively stable, but the magnitude is variable.
